note: Every key of the skald: configuration section, in ONE place (WORKPLAN-BUNDLES.md T7c step 0c). ConfigurationSpecTest holds the Java classes to this file -- every key here is read by the code and every key the code reads is here, with the same default -- and generates from it schemas/config/skald-config.schema.json and the reference in docs/CONFIGURATION.md, failing when either has drifted. Upstream's proxy: section is not described here; ShinyProxy documents it. Packaged onto the classpath (pom.xml) for the startup checks. NOT a JSON Schema; the generated file is.

conventions.names: kebab-case. Spring's relaxed binding also accepts an environment variable (SKALD_BUILDS_MAX_RUNNING) and, inside the map sections, snake_case for the same key.
conventions.duration: A duration with its unit: 300s, 20m, 3h, or ISO-8601 PT5M. A bare number is SECONDS everywhere under skald.*, including the worker's durations, where Spring alone would read milliseconds. parser settings-seconds: whole seconds only (a lease or deadline is kept to the second); parser spring: Spring's converter, sub-second values allowed.
conventions.size: A size with its unit: 64MB, 2GB, 512B. A bare number is refused: '64' meant as megabytes would otherwise be 64 bytes.
conventions.secret: A secret is never written into the file: give it as ${VARIABLE} from the environment, or through Spring's configtree: import of mounted files (/run/secrets). It is never logged; an error about it never repeats its value.
conventions.scope: deployment: every instance must agree (a shared database counts it); instance: this process and its Docker host only.
conventions.parsers: settings / settings-seconds: publisher.config.Settings inside a section parser that refuses unknown keys; spring: Spring's binder on a typed class; value: a single @Value or Environment read; extraction-limits: spec/extraction-limits-v1.json's own parser.

keys.description: The S3-compatible object store (MinIO, Ceph, AWS S3) holding bundles and build logs. Unset: the publishing layer's storage is off and the application boots as upstream.
The store's region; most self-hosted stores accept any value.
The store's access key id. Required with endpoint.
The store's secret key. Required with endpoint.
Path-style bucket addressing. On by default, unlike the SDK: a self-hosted store behind one hostname has no wildcard DNS. Turn off for AWS S3.
Refuse to start when the dispatcher override that runtime-added content needs could not be installed. false starts anyway, and content published at run time will not open.
App builds running at once across the whole deployment, counted in the database.
Builds that may wait (QUEUED) across every content item. May be raised, never removed.
Queued, running and publishing builds one publisher may hold at once.
How long a build's claim lasts without renewal before the reaper interrupts it. Long enough to outlast a stalled host: a holder survives a stall of lease minus renew-every.
How often a running build renews its claim; at most half the lease.
A build's wall-clock deadline; past it the build is TIMED_OUT.
Shared Linux binaries for R packages: compile each package once in a sandbox and serve it from forge. Off until the deployment's security review (WORKPLAN T7b); needs the worker and forge-url.
Package compiles running at once, beside the app builds.
Claims per package before it is FAILED and its apps keep restoring it from source.
How long a compile's claim lasts without renewal.
How often a compile renews its claim; at most half the lease.
One compile's wall-clock deadline. Large packages (duckdb) compile for well over an hour on a busy host.
forge's base URL, ending in /. Unset: shared binaries are off. No credentials, query or fragment in it.
forge's repository for the binaries.
forge's write token, scoped to bin/linux/<codename>-<arch>/contrib/<rminor>/** of the binary repository. Required with forge-url. Never handed to any container.
How long forge's platform registration is trusted before it is read again.
Connecting to forge and each small exchange.
One binary's upload, which grows with the binary.
forge's CRAN proxy member (never the group, which also serves hosted packages), ending in /, from which sources are verified against the public index. Unset: nothing is verified.
The largest package index read.
The largest source tarball read.
A source tarball's largest expanded size.
Connecting to the source repository.
One source or index transfer.
How long a fetched index is reused.
When the index is behind the lock, the first retry; it doubles from there.
The longest wait between retries of an index behind the lock.
How long after the first try a package whose index stays behind is refused INDEX_BEHIND; forge caches a proxy's index for 24 hours by default.
Also build archived versions the index no longer lists, trusting their first fetch (its SHA-256 is recorded and never changes).
Run builds on this instance's Docker host. Needs a database, object storage and every key the worker marks required.
This instance's name on the builds it claims. Unset: the host name.
The build worker image (images/buildkit-worker), by digest.
The egress gateway image (images/egress-gateway), by digest.
The registry's host name as the worker reaches it (port 5000); built images and the published bases live there.
The registry as this instance reaches it, http(s)://host[:port], for publication's digest check. The credential travels in a Basic header: prefer https or an address on this host.
The registry user builds push as.
That user's password.
Docker networks the gateway joins to reach the registry and the mirrors.
Hosts of the package repositories the gateway lets a build reach.
Hosts of private package mirrors the gateway lets a build reach.
The CRAN mirror R builds restore from (forge's CRAN group); its host must be in repos or private-mirrors.
The PyPI simple index Python builds install from; its host must be in repos or private-mirrors.
The CRAN mirror has forge's Linux binary layout (<cran-mirror>__linux__/<codename>/latest). Off by default: a mirror without it answers 404 and renv does not fall back to source.
The published-bases file dev/publish-bases.py wrote: each base's digest in the registry.
A writable directory this instance alone extracts bundles into; locked at startup.
The architecture this host builds for.
Each build's workspace quota. At least 1GB; a cold R build holds the extracted base, BuildKit's snapshots and the compiled library.
How often a running build's stop and log are checked; at most half the coordinator's renew-every.
How long a stopped build is given to wind down before its worker is removed.
The build loop's pause when the queue is empty.
How often the reconciliation sweep removes what no live attempt owns.
How long after a build ends the sweep leaves its attempt alone; longer than settle and the disposal's close wait.
Ready workers per published base, warmed ahead of any build. 0: every build launches its own. Each idle one holds a worker, a gateway, a loop device and a workspace image.
How long a ready worker is kept before a fresh one replaces it.
The object store bucket holding bundles.
The object store bucket holding build logs.

included.description: The bundle extraction bounds, one key per bound in that file (its name with - for _), each a whole number in the unit its name carries, at most its absolute_max. They keep that file's names: the T5 gate's corpus and oracle are written against them.
